draft.title: Transformations on the Cartesian plane
card: Slide every point the same distance in the same direction. Add to \(x\) to move right and to \(y\) to move up. Moving 3 right and 2 down takes \((1, 4)\) to \((4, 2)\).
Flip the shape over a line, as in a mirror. In the \(x\)-axis, \(y\) changes sign and \(x\) stays. In the \(y\)-axis, \(x\) changes sign and \(y\) stays.
Turn the shape about the origin. A half turn (\(180^{\circ}\)) changes the sign of both \(x\) and \(y\), so \((3, 1)\) goes to \((-3, -1)\).
Translations, reflections and rotations move a shape but keep its size and shape the same.
draft.remember: Work out what happens to \(x\) and \(y\): added to, sign changed, or both changed.

a.q: The point \((4, -3)\) is reflected in the \(x\)-axis. What are its new coordinates?
a.why: A reflection in the \(x\)-axis changes the sign of \(y\) and keeps \(x\). So \(-3\) becomes 3 and the point is \((4, 3)\). \((-4, -3)\) is tempting, but that changes \(x\), which is a reflection in the \(y\)-axis.
a.clue: The \(x\)-axis is a horizontal line. Which coordinate flips across it?

b.q: Triangle vertex \(P(-2, 5)\) is translated 4 right and 3 down, then the new point is rotated a half turn about the origin. Where does \(P\) finish?
b.why: Translating gives \((-2 + 4, 5 - 3) = (2, 2)\). A half turn changes both signs, so the point finishes at \((-2, -2)\). \((2, 2)\) is the point after the translation only, before the half turn.
b.clue: Do the slide first, then change both signs.
